tournament.about.event: Heading of the About section when only the event has a description. `<link>` wraps the event's name, linked to its page.
tournament.about.eventLink: Link under the bracket's own description to the event's. `{name}` is the event.
tournament.about.own: Heading of the bracket's own description.
tournament.advancement.addBand: Button: add a band; the plus sign is part of the label.
tournament.advancement.allPlayers: Label of the Remaining band when it is the only band.
tournament.advancement.andBelow: An open-ended band: {from} and every place after it. {from} is a number or an ordinal (5, 5th).
tournament.advancement.badge.bracket: Where a finisher goes: a bracket with no winners or losers side.
tournament.advancement.badge.eliminated: In a pool's Advances column: this finisher goes no further.
tournament.advancement.badge.losers: Where a finisher goes: the losers side of a double-elimination bracket.
tournament.advancement.badge.winners: Where a finisher goes: the winners side of a double-elimination bracket.
tournament.advancement.band.next: Label of every band after the first: the next places.
tournament.advancement.band.place: Beside a band's size; {range} is a place or a range of places (3, 3–4).
tournament.advancement.band.places: Beside the Remaining band; {range} is an open range (5 and below).
tournament.advancement.band.top: Label of the first band: the top places.
tournament.advancement.destination.loser: A double-elimination destination's losers side; {name} is the stage's name.
tournament.advancement.destination.winne: A double-elimination destination's winners side; {name} is the stage's name.
tournament.advancement.eliminated: Under a band with no destination ticked.
tournament.advancement.fromLosers: A cut as a phrase: {n} players from the losers side.
tournament.advancement.fromWinners: A cut as a phrase: {n} players from the winners side.
tournament.advancement.goesTo: Label over the destinations a band routes to.
tournament.advancement.ofEachPool: A band as a phrase for a multi-pool stage; {range} is a band phrase (Top 2).
tournament.advancement.onward: An open-ended band on the plan: {from} is an ordinal (5th).
tournament.advancement.places: Accessible name of the field holding how many places a band covers.
tournament.advancement.range: A range of places: {from} and {to} are numbers or ordinals; the dash is an en dash.
tournament.advancement.remaining: Label of the band covering everyone past the sized bands.
tournament.advancement.splitEvenly: Under a band with {n} destinations ticked (always more than one).
tournament.advancement.title: Heading of the advancement editor.
tournament.advancement.top: A band as a phrase: the top {n} places.
tournament.banding.approx: How many players a placement band is expected to hold; {n} is the estimate, marked approximate.
tournament.banding.approxPerBracket: The same estimate when the band draws from several brackets; {survivors} is how many advance from each.
tournament.bracket.advancesHeading: Heading over a bracket's Advances column: where its players go. `{label}` is the destination stage; the letter marks the winners (W) or losers (L) side.
tournament.bracket.characterFilter: Accessible name of the row of character buttons that fade out sets without that character.
tournament.bracket.characterFilter.all: Character filter button: show every set.
tournament.bracket.characterFilter.label: Label before the character filter buttons.
tournament.bracket.ending.advances: Heading over the column of players a bracket sends on to the next stage, when the bracket names no destination.
tournament.bracket.ending.top: Heading over the column of players a bracket sends on when it stops at a cut: the top n finishers go through.
tournament.bracket.fedBy: In a set's dialog, a player not decided yet: the winner or loser of set number `{n}`.
tournament.bracket.fedBy.short: The same on a bracket card, kept to a letter and the set number: W for winner, L for loser.
tournament.bracket.game: Tooltip on a game number in the bracket; {n} is the number.
tournament.bracket.gameLive: Tooltip on a game number in the bracket while that game is being played; {n} is the number.
tournament.bracket.gameQueued: Tooltip on a game number in the bracket while that game waits for the stream; {n} is the number.
tournament.bracket.inSets: Under a player who went through: their set record. `<b>` wraps the figures.
tournament.bracket.onStream: Read by screen readers on a bracket card whose set is on a stream.
tournament.bracket.round.grandFinals: Name of the Grand Finals set of a double elimination bracket, where the winners side's champion meets the losers side's champion. Shown on set cards, stream overlays and the queue.
tournament.bracket.round.losers: A set's position when its round is unknown: the losers side of a double elimination bracket, where players who have lost once still play.
tournament.bracket.round.losersFinals: Column heading in a bracket: the last round of the losers side. Plural in English by convention.
tournament.bracket.round.losersQuarters: Column heading in a bracket: the losers side's quarter-final round, two rounds before its final.
tournament.bracket.round.losersSemis: Column heading in a bracket: the losers side's semi-final round, one round before its final.
tournament.bracket.round.numbered: Column heading in a bracket for an early round with no conventional name; {n} is the round number.
tournament.bracket.round.sided: A set's position on stream overlays, the queue and a set's dialog: the side of the bracket (winners, for players unbeaten so far, or losers) and {n}, the round number on that side.
tournament.bracket.round.tiebreak: Name of a tiebreak set played after the bracket to separate two players tied on a placement, when the placement it decides is not recorded.
tournament.bracket.round.tiebreakPlace: Name of a tiebreak set played after the bracket to separate two players tied on a placement; {place} is that placement as an ordinal (5th).
tournament.bracket.round.winners: A set's position when its round is unknown: the winners side of a bracket, where players are unbeaten so far.
tournament.bracket.round.winnersFinal: Column heading in a bracket: the last round of the winners side, before Grand Finals.
tournament.bracket.round.winnersQuarters: Column heading in a bracket: the winners side's quarter-final round, two rounds before its final.
tournament.bracket.round.winnersSemis: Column heading in a bracket: the winners side's semi-final round, one round before its final.
tournament.bracket.seed: Under a player who went through: their seed. `<b>` wraps the number.
tournament.bracket.setDetails: Tooltip of a bracket card: opens the set's details. The state says whether it is being played and whether it is on stream.
tournament.bracket.side.single: Heading over a single-elimination bracket, which has no losers side to contrast with.
tournament.bracket.traceHint: Faint hint over the bracket: pressing a player's picture highlights their path through it.
tournament.champion: Small label beside the tournament's or a pool's winner.
tournament.changeLog.column.by: Column heading of the change log: who made the change.
tournament.changeLog.column.description: Column heading of the change log: what changed.
tournament.changeLog.column.type: Column heading of the change log: the kind of change.
tournament.changeLog.column.when: Column heading of the change log: when the change was made.
tournament.changeLog.empty: The change log when nothing has been corrected.
tournament.changeLog.type.detailsUpdate: A kind of change: the tournament's details were edited.
tournament.changeLog.type.dqUpdate: A kind of change: a disqualification was added or removed.
tournament.changeLog.type.gameLogRecorde: A kind of change: game-by-game results were recorded for a set.
tournament.changeLog.type.placementCorre: A kind of change: a final placement was corrected.
tournament.changeLog.type.playerMerge: A kind of change: two player records were joined into one.
tournament.changeLog.type.playerSubstitu: A kind of change: one player was swapped for another.
tournament.changeLog.type.scoreCorrectio: A kind of change: a set's score was corrected.
tournament.checkIn.inNamed: Accessible name of the check-in toggle. `{name}` is the entrant.
tournament.checkIn.openNow: Status line in the running-sets controls while check-in is open; the emphasised word is the state.
tournament.checkIn.outNamed: Accessible name of the check-in toggle when the entrant is already checked in.
tournament.correction.recordWinner: Accessible name of the button that records a side as the set's winner; {name} is the side.
tournament.criteria.blurb.by: Beside the filter word by: in a tournament archive's filter list. Lower case, no full stop.
tournament.criteria.blurb.entrants: Beside the filter word entrants: in a tournament archive's filter list; the field is everyone who entered. Lower case, no full stop.
tournament.criteria.blurb.prize: Beside the filter word prize: in a tournament archive's filter list; the pot is the prize money. Lower case, no full stop.
tournament.criteria.blurb.ran: Beside the filter word ran: in a tournament archive's filter list. Lower case, no full stop.
tournament.criteria.blurb.series: Beside the filter word series: in a tournament archive's filter list. Lower case, no full stop.
tournament.criteria.blurb.strength: Beside the filter word strength: in a tournament archive's filter list. Lower case, no full stop.
tournament.criteria.blurb.won: Beside the filter word won: in a tournament archive's filter list. Lower case, no full stop.
tournament.crosstable.column.advances: Column heading of a pool's crosstable: where each player goes next.
tournament.crosstable.column.place: Column heading of a pool's crosstable: finishing place.
tournament.crosstable.column.player: Column heading of a pool's crosstable: the player.
tournament.crosstable.onStream: Tooltip of a crosstable cell whose set is on a stream. `{title}` is the cell's own tooltip.
tournament.crosstable.onStreamSuffix: Read by screen readers after a live crosstable cell's figure when it is on a stream; it continues the cell, so it starts with a comma.
tournament.crosstable.title.live: Tooltip of a crosstable cell for a set being played. `{score}` is the score so far, `{round}` a number.
tournament.crosstable.title.result: Tooltip of a crosstable cell for a finished set, from the row player's side. `{score}` is the score; DQ means a disqualification.
tournament.crosstable.title.scheduled: Tooltip of a crosstable cell for a set not played yet. `{score}` is a score entered but not reported.
tournament.cut.advancingSummary: Under the depth picker: {n} players advance in all, {winners} from the winners side and, when {de} is yes, {losers} from the losers side.
tournament.cut.losersOnly.named: Warning under the cut editor; {stages} is a comma-separated list of the stage names that would take entrants only on the losers side.
tournament.cut.losersSurvivors: Label of the losers side's survivors in the cut editor.
tournament.cut.noneProjected: Under the stops-early option when nobody is projected into the stage.
tournament.cut.playsOut: Ending option: the bracket plays to a champion.
tournament.cut.seats: A depth option on a double-elimination bracket: {label} is the depth (Top 8), {winners} and {losers} how many seats each side holds; W and L abbreviate winners and losers.
tournament.cut.stopsEarly: Ending option: the bracket stops at a depth.
tournament.cut.stopsEarly.note: Explainer under the stops-early option; {de} is yes for a double-elimination bracket.
tournament.cut.survivors: Label of the surviving side of a single-elimination cut.
tournament.cut.title: Heading of the ending switch on a bracket: plays out, or stops early.
tournament.cut.winnersSurvivors: Label of the winners side's survivors in the cut editor.
tournament.delete.action: The confirm button of the delete-tournament dialog, and the title of the delete row in the Advanced node.
tournament.delete.description: Body of the delete-tournament dialog, above a box where the person types a word to confirm.
tournament.delete.open: Button in the Advanced node that opens the delete-tournament dialog; the ellipsis says a dialog follows.
tournament.delete.row.description: Under the Delete tournament row in the Advanced node, beside the button that opens the dialog.
tournament.delete.title: Title of the delete-tournament dialog.
tournament.dq.confirm.setNote: Dialog body under the set-disqualification question. DQ is the tournament term for a disqualification.
tournament.dq.confirm.setTitle: Question asked before an entrant is disqualified from one set; {name} is the entrant.
tournament.dq.confirm.tournamentNote: Dialog body under the tournament-disqualification question.
tournament.dq.confirm.tournamentTitle: Question asked before an entrant is disqualified from the whole tournament; {name} is the entrant.
tournament.dqTimer.help: Under the DQ timer default setting. A DQ is a disqualification; the countdown only prompts the organiser when it runs out. The last sentence shows only when the viewer can edit ({editable} is yes): the value saves when focus leaves the field.
tournament.dqTimer.minutes.label: Accessible name of the number field holding the DQ timer's default, in minutes.
tournament.dqTimer.minutes.unit: Unit after the DQ timer field: minutes, abbreviated.
tournament.dqTimer.title: Heading of the setting for how long the disqualification countdown runs by default when a player does not turn up.
tournament.endStage.confirm.action: Button that confirms ending the stage.
tournament.endStage.confirm.finalises: Confirmation question when ending the last stage.
tournament.endStage.confirm.multi: Confirmation question when the stage feeds several later stages. `{destList}` names them.
tournament.endStage.confirm.routesNowher: Confirmation question when the stage feeds no later stage.
tournament.endStage.confirm.single: Confirmation question when the stage feeds one later stage. `{destList}` names it.
tournament.endStage.message.finalises: What ending the last stage does.
tournament.endStage.message.multi: What ending the stage does when it feeds several later stages. `{destList}` names them.
tournament.endStage.message.routesNowher: What ending the stage does when it feeds no later stage.
tournament.endStage.message.single: What ending the stage does when it feeds one later stage. `{destList}` names it.
tournament.entrant.dq.tag: The small upper-case tag beside a disqualified entrant's placement. Disqualified, as the bracket abbreviates it.
tournament.entrant.fact.checkIn: The fact's label in the entrant dialog; its value is `tournament.entrant.fact.in` or `.notIn`.
tournament.entrant.fact.in: A fact line on the entrant dialog: the entrant IS in the current stage's bracket. Beside `tournament.entrant.fact.notIn`.
tournament.entrant.fact.notIn: The entrant is NOT in the current stage's bracket.
tournament.entrant.fact.placed: The label of the entrant's final placement, shown before a number or `tournament.entrant.none`.
tournament.entrant.fact.walkUp: How the entrant got in: at the venue, with no account (`tournament.walkUp.add`), as against `tournament.entrant.fact.entered`.
tournament.entrant.manageNamed: Accessible name of the button that opens an entrant's dialog. `{name}` is the entrant.
tournament.entrant.none: No value: no placement yet, no player record, no seed. A bare word in a facts list.
tournament.entrant.playerLabel: The label ahead of the entrant's member names. `{kind}` is `team` or `solo`.
tournament.entrant.playerRecordOf: Under the entrant's name once the stage has started: the heading and the record itself. `{kind}` is `team` or `solo`; `{players}` is the record, already formatted.
tournament.entrant.rankAndRatingIn: Under the entrant's figures: which community board the rank and rating are read from. `{scope}` is the community's name.
tournament.entrant.ratingIn: As `tournament.entrant.rankAndRatingIn`, for an entrant with a rating but no rank yet.
tournament.entrant.replace.creating: The button's text while a new player record is being created.
tournament.entrant.replace.summary: Confirms a replacement before it is saved: `{from}` and `{to}` are player names; `<b>` marks the new one. `{teamName}` is `follows` for a team whose name was derived from its players' names, `keeps` for a team with a name of its own, `none` for a solo entrant.
tournament.entrant.seedNumber: A player's seed. `{seed}` is a number.
tournament.error.allEvents: Link from the error page to a game's tournaments. `{game}` is the game's short address name.
tournament.error.body: On the page shown when a tournament fails to load: the results themselves are safe.
tournament.error.eyebrow: Small label over the error heading: the kind of page that failed.
tournament.error.retry: On the error page: try again, and quote the reference shown under it if it keeps failing.
tournament.error.title: Heading of the page shown when a tournament fails to load.
tournament.format.backfill.hasStages: Why the stage backfill skipped a tournament. Read in the backfill's report by the operator who ran it; lower case.
tournament.format.backfill.lowConfidence: Why the stage backfill skipped an old import. {type} is the stage format's id (single_elimination), {why} the reading's reason, itself from tournament.format.inference.*.
tournament.format.backfill.multiStage: Why the stage backfill skipped an old import. {count} is a number of sets. Read in the backfill's report by the operator who ran it.
tournament.format.backfill.noSets: Why the stage backfill skipped an old import: it has no sets. Read in the backfill's report by the operator who ran it; lower case, it follows the tournament's id.
tournament.format.backfill.standings: Why the stage backfill skipped an old import. {type} is the stage format's id (round_robin, swiss), {why} the reading's reason, itself from tournament.format.inference.*.
tournament.format.doubleElimination: A stage format: a bracket where a player is out after two losses.
tournament.format.inference.doubleElimin: A line in an operator's stage-backfill report: why an imported bracket with no recorded format reads as double elimination.
tournament.format.inference.losersTag: A line in an operator's stage-backfill report: why an imported bracket reads as double elimination. A losers or grand-finals side exists only in double elimination.
tournament.format.inference.noSets: A line in an operator's stage-backfill report: why an imported bracket's format cannot be read. It has no finished sets.
tournament.format.inference.roundRobin: A line in an operator's stage-backfill report: why an imported bracket reads as a round robin.
tournament.format.inference.roundRobinPo: A line in an operator's stage-backfill report: why an imported bracket reads as a round robin run as several pools. {pools} is how many, always 2 or more.
tournament.format.inference.singleElimin: A line in an operator's stage-backfill report: why an imported bracket reads as single elimination. {entrants} is how many entrants played in it.
tournament.format.inference.swiss: A line in an operator's stage-backfill report: why an imported bracket reads as Swiss. {losses} is the most losses any entrant has (3 or more); {fewest} and {most} are the fewest and most sets any entrant played.
tournament.format.inference.tooFew: A line in an operator's stage-backfill report: why an imported bracket's format cannot be read. {entrants} is how many entrants played, always fewer than 3.
tournament.format.roundRobin: A stage format: a pool where everyone plays everyone.
tournament.format.singleElimination: A stage format: a bracket where a player is out after one loss.
tournament.format.swiss: A stage format: a pool paired round by round on records (the Swiss system).
tournament.game.capture.importedIntro: Intro above the game log of an imported set, where games can be added by hand.
tournament.game.character.none: Empty result in the character picker's search.
tournament.game.character.search: Placeholder of the character picker's search.
tournament.game.character.set: Accessible name of the character picker button when no character is chosen yet.
tournament.game.character.unknown: Stands in for a character nobody recorded for this game.
tournament.game.character.unset: Picker option that clears the character back to unknown.
tournament.game.corrected: Note beside a game in an imported set's log that someone fixed by hand, when who fixed it is not known.
tournament.game.correctedBy: Note beside a game in an imported set's log that someone fixed by hand; {name} is who fixed it.
tournament.game.correction.intro: Intro above an imported set's game log, where a game's character or stage can be fixed.
tournament.game.empty: Empty game log of a set being reported.
tournament.game.loading: Shown while a set's game log loads.
tournament.game.needsPlayers: Shown instead of the game log while one of the set's two slots is still empty.
tournament.game.remove.confirm: Confirm button of the remove-game dialog.
tournament.game.remove.confirmTitle: Title of the dialog confirming a game's removal from a set; {n} is the game's number in the set.
tournament.game.remove.hint: Tooltip on a game's remove button.
tournament.game.remove.importedNote: Remove-game dialog, on an imported set: the source's result is kept.
tournament.game.remove.label: Accessible name of a game's remove button; {n} is the game's number in the set.
tournament.game.remove.reportedNote: Remove-game dialog, on a set already reported here.
tournament.game.score.label: Heading of a game's optional score picker (stocks or rounds left).
tournament.game.score.set: Accessible name of a game's score picker.
tournament.game.short: Short for Game {n}, between the two players' buttons while logging a set; kept very short.
tournament.game.stage: Placeholder of the free-text stage field when the game has no stage list.
tournament.game.stage.label: Heading of a game's optional stage picker.
tournament.game.stage.named: Accessible name of a game's stage button; {label} is the stage's name.
tournament.game.stage.other: Placeholder of the free-text stage field below the game's stage list.
tournament.game.stage.set: Accessible name of a game's stage button when no stage is chosen.
tournament.game.won: Accessible name and tooltip of the tick marking which player won a game.
tournament.game.wonBy: Accessible name of the button a player's name sits on while logging a set: pressing it records that {name} won game {n}.
tournament.gameCorrection.action: Title and confirm button of the dialog that moves a tournament to a different game (the verb: correct the game).
tournament.gameCorrection.checking: Shown while the move to another game is being previewed.
tournament.gameCorrection.clearsPlayedAs: Consequence of moving a tournament to another game: {n} character picks belong to the old game and are cleared.
tournament.gameCorrection.field: Label of the picker choosing which game the tournament should be under (the right game).
tournament.gameCorrection.intro: Intro of the dialog that moves a tournament to a different game.
tournament.gameCorrection.movesTo: Consequence of moving a tournament to another game: its new address. {path} is the URL path, inside <code>; {slugChanged} is yes when the old address was taken and a new one was made.
tournament.gameCorrection.open: Button opening the dialog that moves a tournament to a different game.
tournament.gameCorrection.placeholder: Placeholder of the picker choosing the right game.
tournament.gameCorrection.rerate.deferre: Consequence line when a tournament's game is corrected and the boards recalculate overnight; {from} is the old game, {to} the new.
tournament.gameCorrection.rerate.inline: Consequence line when a tournament's game is corrected and the boards recalculate at once; {from} is the old game, {to} the new.
tournament.gameCorrection.rerate.none: Consequence line when a tournament's game is corrected and no board is affected.
tournament.gameCorrection.row.descriptio: Under the Correct game row in the Advanced node. {game} is the name of the game the tournament is filed under now.
tournament.gameCorrection.sourceLabel: Advisory in the move-to-another-game dialog. {source} is the import source (start.gg, Challonge…), {game} is the game it names, in <b>; {catalogued} is no when Dizzy does not list that game.
tournament.lens.goToEvent: Button to the event page, where players enter.
tournament.lens.noEntrants: The entrant list when there is nobody to show.
tournament.lens.registrationOpen: Heading before the bracket exists, while players can still enter.
tournament.masthead.back.all: Back link at the top of an imported tournament: the list of tournaments.
tournament.masthead.back.event: Back link at the top of a tournament: its event.
tournament.masthead.entered: In the line under the name, before play: how many entered. `<b>` wraps the number.
tournament.masthead.inGames: The champion's game record, wins then losses.
tournament.masthead.inSets: The champion's set record. `{record}` is wins–losses.
tournament.masthead.next: Label over the sets called to play next.
tournament.masthead.organisedBy: In the line under the name, before the organisers' names.
tournament.masthead.played: In the line under the name: how many have played so far, of how many registered. `<b>` wraps the first number.
tournament.masthead.prize: In the line under the name: the prize pool. `<b>` wraps the amount, already formatted.
tournament.masthead.ranked: The tournament counts toward player ratings.
tournament.masthead.sets: In the line under the name: sets finished. `<b>` wraps the number.
tournament.masthead.unranked: The tournament does not count toward player ratings.
tournament.notFound.body: On the missing-tournament page: an unpublished tournament looks the same as a missing one.
tournament.notFound.help: On the missing-tournament page: what to do if the link came from a host.
tournament.notFound.title: Heading of the missing-tournament page.
tournament.page.delistedBanner: Banner for moderators on a tournament hidden from the public site.
tournament.page.draftBanner: Banner for staff on a tournament not published yet.
tournament.page.source: Label before the site the tournament was imported from.
tournament.pairing.heading.asked: Heading of the partner band when someone has invited the viewer to team up.
tournament.pairing.heading.canTeamUp: Heading of the partner band in a bracket where solo entrants and teams play together.
tournament.pairing.heading.needsPartner: Heading of the partner band in a doubles bracket where the viewer has no partner yet.
tournament.pairing.heading.teamed: Heading of the partner band once the viewer has a partner.
tournament.pairing.host.drop: Organiser's button dropping an unpaired entrant from a doubles bracket.
tournament.pairing.host.drop.confirm: Asks the organiser to confirm dropping an unpaired entrant.
tournament.pairing.host.drop.yes: Confirm button for dropping an unpaired entrant.
tournament.pairing.host.dropped: Heading of the list of entrants the organiser dropped for having no partner.
tournament.pairing.host.droppedNote: Below the dropped entrants: a dropped entrant can be put back.
tournament.pairing.host.heading: Heading of the organiser's band listing entrants with no partner.
tournament.pairing.host.nobodyLeft: Organiser's band, when an unpaired entrant has nobody left to pair with.
tournament.pairing.host.pairWith: Organiser's button pairing the chosen entrant with {name}.
tournament.pairing.host.picking: Organiser's band after choosing an entrant to pair; {name} is that entrant, in <b>.
tournament.pairing.host.putBack: Organiser's button putting a dropped entrant back in the bracket.
tournament.pairing.host.ready: Organiser's band once every entrant has a partner.
tournament.pairing.host.stillPaying: Beside an entrant whose payment has not gone through yet.
tournament.pairing.host.unpaired: Organiser's band: {n} entrants have no partner in a doubles bracket.
tournament.pairing.intro.open: Partner band in a bracket seating solo entrants and teams together, for a viewer already entered.
tournament.pairing.intro.openInvited: Partner band in a bracket seating solo entrants and teams together, for a viewer invited but not entered.
tournament.pairing.intro.teams: Partner band in a doubles bracket, for a viewer already entered.
tournament.pairing.intro.teamsInvited: Partner band in a doubles bracket, for a viewer invited but not entered.
tournament.pairing.invite: Button inviting a person to be the viewer's partner.
tournament.pairing.invite.retract: Button taking back an invite the viewer sent.
tournament.pairing.invites.received: Heading of the partner invites sent to the viewer.
tournament.pairing.invites.sent: Heading of the partner invites the viewer sent.
tournament.pairing.looking: Heading of the list of people the viewer can invite as a partner.
tournament.pairing.looking.allAsked: When the viewer has invited everyone still free.
tournament.pairing.looking.nobodyFree: When nobody else registered for the event is free to partner.
tournament.pairing.notEntered: Beside a person in the partner list who has not entered this bracket yet.
tournament.pairing.search.label: Accessible name of the search box over the people the viewer can invite.
tournament.pairing.search.more: Below a shortened list of people to invite; {n} more are hidden.
tournament.pairing.search.none: Empty result of the partner search.
tournament.pairing.with: Between the viewer's team name and their partner's name.
tournament.participation.confirmEnter: Confirms that the host enters their own tournament as a player.

tournament.settings.description: Label of the tournament's description field.
tournament.settings.description.placehol: Placeholder of the description field, on two paragraphs. The Markdown examples are what a person types (**bold**, [links](…), - for a bullet), so keep the symbols as they are.
tournament.settings.health.addStage: Link on a setup health item saying the tournament has no stages: opens the Stages settings.
tournament.settings.health.openSignups: Link on a setup health item saying nobody has entered: opens the event's registration settings.
tournament.settings.health.setDate: Link on a setup health item saying the tournament has no date: opens the Details settings.
tournament.settings.name: Label of the tournament's own name field in its Details settings.
tournament.settings.name.help: Under the tournament name field. {name} is the name it gets when left blank, the game and format ("Lethal League Blaze Singles").
tournament.settings.node.changelog: A node in the tournament page's Settings tree, and its panel's title: the log of corrections staff made.
tournament.settings.node.prizePool: A node in the tournament page's Settings tree, and its panel's title: what each placement pays.
tournament.settings.node.queue: A node in the tournament page's Settings tree, and its panel's title: the sets waiting to go on stream, in order.
tournament.settings.node.runningSets: A node in the tournament page's Settings tree, and its panel's title: how sets are run on the day (check-in, stations, score reporting).
tournament.settings.node.stages: A node in the tournament page's Settings tree, and its panel's title: the stages the tournament is played in (pools, a bracket).
tournament.settings.node.streams: A node in the tournament page's Settings tree, and its panel's title: the streams attached to the event and the overlay addresses.
tournament.settings.publicUrl: Label of the field holding the last part of the tournament's address on this site; the fixed part before it shows beside the field.
tournament.settings.publicUrl.locked: Under the public URL field once it can no longer be changed.
tournament.settings.roles.note: Under the list of a tournament's own hosts. {listed} is yes when the event has event-wide organisers, and {names} is their names, joined by commas. <link> wraps the name of the event page's settings node, and is a link to it.
tournament.settings.saveUrl: Button beside a URL field: save that one field.
tournament.settings.series: Label of the field that attaches the event to a series (a run of recurring events).
tournament.settings.series.back: Button: leave the new-series fields and go back to searching.
tournament.settings.series.confirm: Button: accept the new series' name and slug. Nothing is saved until the form's own save.
tournament.settings.series.create: The last entry in the series search results: make a new series with the name typed. {name} is what was typed. The plus sign is part of the label.
tournament.settings.series.name: Label of a new series' name field.
tournament.settings.series.name.placehol: Placeholder of a new series' name field.
tournament.settings.series.new: Beside a series that is chosen but not yet created: marks it as new, then its address. {slug} is the address word; keep the slash.
tournament.settings.series.search: Placeholder of the series search box.
tournament.settings.series.search.orCrea: Placeholder of the series search box for someone who may also make a new series.
tournament.settings.series.slug: Label of a new series' slug field: the word used in its web address.
tournament.settings.series.slug.placehol: Placeholder of a new series' slug field.
tournament.settings.slug.invalid: Error when the typed address word is not valid. The limits are a length from 3 to 60 characters.
tournament.settings.startDate: Label of the tournament's start date and time field.
tournament.settings.viewOnly: Leads a settings panel that site staff can see but not change. A TO is a tournament organiser.
tournament.setupHealth.bracketDraft: A row on the tournament's setup checklist, read by its host.
tournament.setupHealth.noDate: A row on the tournament's setup checklist.
tournament.setupHealth.noEntrants: A row on the tournament's setup checklist.
tournament.setupHealth.noStages: A row on the tournament's setup checklist. A stage is one phase of the bracket (pools, then a top cut).
tournament.setupHealth.streamNotRouted: A row on the tournament's setup checklist; routing a stream points a broadcast at this bracket.
tournament.setupHealth.unseeded: A row on the tournament's setup checklist; seeding is the starting order of its entrants.
tournament.stage.awaiting.body: Explains why a stage cannot open yet: the stages before it must finish.
tournament.stage.awaiting.title: Heading when the stages before this one are not finished; each is linked after it.
tournament.stage.delete.blocked: Tooltip on a disabled Delete button once play has started.
tournament.stage.delete.confirmTitle: Confirmation question before deleting a stage; {name} is the stage's name.
tournament.stage.fallback: Stands in for a stage's name when it cannot be found.
tournament.stage.format: Field label: a stage's format (one of the four).
tournament.stage.format.clearsBands: Warning under the format field: {to} is the format being picked and {from} the saved one, both format names (tournament.format.*).
tournament.stage.format.dropsLosers: Warning under the format field when a double-elimination stage changes format.
tournament.stage.format.finalPoolsTie: Warning under the format field for a final stage split into {n} pools (always more than one).
tournament.stage.format.kindResets: Warning under the format field when a stage changes between a pool and a bracket format.
tournament.stage.format.pairing: Field label: how a Swiss stage pairs its first round.
tournament.stage.format.poolCountResets: Warning under the format field when the pool count changes.
tournament.stage.format.pools: Field label: how many pools a stage splits into.
tournament.stage.format.rounds: Field label: how many rounds a Swiss stage plays.
tournament.stage.heading: Eyebrow over the stage dialog's title: {position} is this stage's number in the order, {count} how many stages there are.
tournament.stage.lockedNote: Note in the stage dialog once play has started.
tournament.stage.losersOnly.badge: Badge on a stage card: the rule a double-elimination stage breaks when nobody is routed into its winners side. A formula; keep it as it is.
tournament.stage.losersOnly.named: Warning under the advancement editor; {stages} is a comma-separated list of the stage names that would take entrants only on the losers side.
tournament.stage.losersOnly.projected: Warning on a stage card: the stage is projected to take entrants only on its losers side.
tournament.stage.noStartTime: On a stage card when no start time is set.
tournament.stage.pairing.fold: A Swiss round-1 pairing method, named by the matchup it makes: seed 1 plays seed 8 in a field of eight.
tournament.stage.pairing.slide: A Swiss round-1 pairing method, named by the matchup it makes: seed 1 plays seed 5 in a field of eight.
tournament.stage.position: Field label: where a new stage sits in the order.
tournament.stage.read.aLaterStage: Stands in for a destination stage that no longer exists.
tournament.stage.read.arrives: An arrivals line: {subject} is who, {source} the stage they come from, {side} the side of this stage they enter or none.
tournament.stage.read.arrivesCut: An arrivals line from a cut: as tournament.stage.read.arrives, with {n} the depth the source bracket stopped at.
tournament.stage.read.finalChampion: The Out: line of a final stage whose winner is the tournament champion.
tournament.stage.read.finalPlaces: The Out: line of a final stage that writes places but no champion.
tournament.stage.read.losersPlaces: Who a band routes from the losers side; {places} is a place range (1st–2nd).
tournament.stage.read.losersSide: A side of a double-elimination stage, mid-line and lower case.
tournament.stage.read.losersSurvivors: Who a cut routes: the players still alive on the losers side.
tournament.stage.read.projectedIn: In a stage card's facts line: about {n} players projected to enter.
tournament.stage.read.projectedInDe: As tournament.stage.read.projectedIn for a double-elimination stage, split into {winners} and {losers}; W and L abbreviate the sides.
tournament.stage.read.rosterEntry: Arrivals line for the stage the roster enters by default.
tournament.stage.read.routeTo: A routing line: {subject} is who (1st–2nd, Winners survivors), {dest} the stage they go to, {side} its side (tournament.stage.read.*Side) or none.
tournament.stage.read.splitWays: Ends a routing line: the band is split across {n} destinations.
tournament.stage.read.stopsAtTop: Leads a routing line for a cut: the depth {n} the bracket stops at.
tournament.stage.read.tiebreaksOn: In a stage's format line when it plays tiebreaks.
tournament.stage.read.winnersPlaces: Who a band routes from the winners side; {places} is a place range (1st–2nd).
tournament.stage.read.winnersSide: A side of a double-elimination stage, mid-line and lower case.
tournament.stage.read.winnersSurvivors: Who a cut routes: the players still alive on the winners side.
tournament.stage.routing: Field label: where a stage's finishers go next.
tournament.stage.routing.discard.title: Confirmation question when leaving the routing editor with unsaved changes.
tournament.stage.routing.in: Label before the list of who arrives at a stage; keep the colon.
tournament.stage.routing.noAdvancementYe: Value of the Routing field when no advancement has been authored.
tournament.stage.routing.noneAuthored: After the Out: label when no advancement has been authored; lower case, mid-line.
tournament.stage.routing.nothingInYet: After the In: label when no earlier stage routes anyone here; lower case, mid-line.
tournament.stage.routing.nothingInYet.ex: Under the Who gets here heading when no earlier stage routes anyone here.
tournament.stage.routing.out: Label before the list of where a stage's finishers go; keep the colon.
tournament.stage.routing.out.champion: Badge on a final stage whose winner is the tournament champion.
tournament.stage.routing.out.final: Badge on a final stage that writes places but no champion.
tournament.stage.routing.whoGetsHere: Heading over the list of who arrives at a stage.
tournament.stage.seedInEntrantsTab: Pointer under the stage setup panel; the emphasised word is the name of the Entrants tab as it appears in the page.
tournament.stage.start.blockedIntro: Before the list of stages that cannot start and why.
tournament.stage.start.configure: Link to the stage's setup when it cannot start yet.
tournament.stage.start.confirm.title: Confirmation question before starting a stage.
tournament.stage.start.notReady: Label of the start band when something blocks the start.
tournament.stage.start.note.rebalancePoo: Hint before starting a pool stage from Settings.
tournament.stage.start.note.seedingList: Hint before starting a pool stage from its own page.
tournament.stage.start.note.seedingTab: Hint before starting a bracket stage from its own page.
tournament.stage.start.note.settingsSeed: Hint before starting a bracket stage from Settings.
tournament.stage.start.ready: Label of the start band when the stage can start.
tournament.stage.starts: Field label: when a stage starts.
tournament.stage.status.inProgress: A stage's state, on a card: running now.
tournament.stage.status.notStarted: A stage's state: not yet started.
tournament.stage.status.pending: A stage's state, on the plan: not yet started.
tournament.stage.status.running: A stage's state, on the plan: running now.
tournament.stage.swiss.max: Helper text under the Swiss rounds field once the maximum is reached; {n} is that maximum, {perPool} the players per pool.
tournament.stage.swiss.proposed: Helper text under the Swiss rounds field before a number is saved; {n} is the proposed number of rounds.
tournament.stage.viewOnly: Note in the stage dialog for someone who may only look.
tournament.stageView.crosstable: Switch option: a pool's crosstable (every player against every other).
tournament.stageView.earlierStage: Stands in for the name of the stage a player came from when it cannot be found.
tournament.stageView.end.allIn: Label of the end-stage band when every set is reported.
tournament.stageView.end.notReady: Label of the end-stage band when something blocks ending.
tournament.stageView.end.topDecided: Label of the end-stage band when the places that advance are decided. `{depth}` is a number.
tournament.stageView.notStarted.body: A stage that has not started, for someone who is not staff.
tournament.stageView.notStarted.title: Heading of a stage that has not started.
tournament.stageView.poolStandings: Heading of one pool's standings. `{name}` is the pool.
tournament.stageView.progress: Label of the stage's progress bar.
tournament.stageView.progress.figures: Beside the progress bar: sets finished of all sets, and the percentage.
tournament.stageView.reported.endHere: Every set is in and the stage can end. `<link>` wraps the link to the stage overview.
tournament.stageView.reported.endLater: This pool is finished, but others are not. `<link>` wraps the link to the stage overview.
tournament.stageView.reported.pool: Heading when one pool has every set reported. `{name}` is the pool.
tournament.stageView.reported.stage: Heading when the whole stage has every set reported.
tournament.stageView.seeded: For staff, before a stage starts, when the field is seeded. `<b>` wraps the number of entrants.
tournament.stageView.standings: Heading, and switch option: the standings.
tournament.stageView.tooFew: Before a stage starts, when fewer than two have entered.
tournament.stageView.unknownEntrant: Stands in for a player's name when it cannot be found.
tournament.stageView.waiting.body: A stage waiting on the stages before it.
tournament.stageView.waiting.title: Heading of a stage waiting on the stages before it.
tournament.stages.add: Button: add a stage; the plus sign is part of the label.
tournament.stages.add.label: Accessible name of the add-stage control.
tournament.stages.create: Button: create the stage the form describes.
tournament.stages.empty: Empty state of the stages list for someone who may only look.
tournament.stages.emptyAddFirst: Empty state of the stages list; {button} is the add-stage button's label, and <b> marks it as a button name.
tournament.stages.intro: Explainer over the stages list in Settings.
tournament.stages.locked.note: Note shown once the tournament has started: stages can no longer change.
tournament.stages.locked.title: Heading of the note shown once the tournament has started.
tournament.standings.column.entrant: Column heading of the standings: the player or team.
tournament.standings.column.games: Column heading of the standings: game record.
tournament.standings.column.lostTo: Column heading of the standings: who beat them.
tournament.standings.column.place: Column heading of the standings: finishing place.
tournament.standings.column.prize: Column heading of the standings: prize money won.
tournament.standings.column.run: Hidden column heading, for screen readers: the button that shows a player's run.
tournament.standings.column.seed: Column heading of the standings: seed.
tournament.standings.column.sets: Column heading of the standings: set record.
tournament.standings.empty: The standings when nothing has been recorded.
tournament.standings.gamesLine: In a player's expanded row: their game record, wins then losses.
tournament.standings.noPositions: An old imported tournament with no bracket positions.
tournament.standings.noSets: In a player's expanded row: they played no sets.
tournament.standings.notBeaten: In the Lost to column: nobody beat them.
tournament.standings.overall: Switch option: standings across the whole tournament.
tournament.standings.provisional.title: Heading of standings that may still change.
tournament.standings.refetch.action: Button that imports the tournament again from its source.
tournament.standings.refetch.anyway: Imports again even though manual corrections will be lost.
tournament.standings.refetch.error: The import failed. `{message}` is the reason, as given.
tournament.standings.refetch.running: The import button while it works.
tournament.standings.refetch.warning: Warns that importing again loses the manual corrections listed under it.
tournament.standings.runToggle: Accessible name of the button that shows or hides a player's run through the tournament.
tournament.standings.setsIn: Accessible name of a player's sets in one stage. `{stage}` names the stage.
tournament.standings.setsPlayed: Accessible name of a player's sets.
tournament.standings.stagePicker: Accessible name of the switch between overall and per-stage standings.
tournament.standings.step.lost: Read by screen readers in a player's run: they lost to the next name.
tournament.standings.step.out: Read by screen readers after a set: it knocked the player out. It continues the line, so it starts with a comma.
tournament.standings.step.won: Read by screen readers in a player's run: they beat the next name.
tournament.start.blocked.perPool: Why a stage cannot start: too few players across its pools; {projected} is how many it has, {required} how many it needs, {pools} how many pools.
tournament.start.blocked.tooFew: Why a single-pool stage cannot start; {n} is how many players it has.
tournament.start.blocked.winnersSide: Why a stage cannot start: a double-elimination bracket with nobody on its winners side.
tournament.stations.busy: Above a stage's sets: how many stations have a set being played on them, out of all of them. {busy} and {total} are numbers.
tournament.stations.empty: In the station list when there are none, for a viewer who cannot add any.
tournament.stations.empty.generate: In the station list when there are none, for the organiser, who can generate them with the button above.
tournament.stations.generate: Button: make the number of stations in the box beside it.
tournament.stations.generate.count: Accessible name of the number box saying how many stations Generate makes.
tournament.stations.inUse: Beside a station that has a set on it, when the set has no player names yet.
tournament.stations.name.label: Accessible name of a station's name field.
tournament.stations.playing: Beside a station that has a set on it: the two players or teams playing. {a} and {b} are their names.
tournament.stations.preferred: Beside a station marked as preferred, in the read-only list.
tournament.stations.preferred.mark: Tooltip of the star button on a station that is not preferred: mark it as preferred.
tournament.stations.preferred.on: Tooltip of the star button on a station that is preferred.
tournament.stations.remove: Tooltip of a station's remove button.
tournament.stations.remove.busy: Tooltip of a station's remove button while a set is being played on it. A Set is one match between two entrants.
tournament.stations.remove.named: Accessible name of a station's remove button. {name} is the station's name.
tournament.stations.title: Heading of the stations list; the count follows it in brackets. A station is one physical setup (a console and screen) matches are played on.
tournament.streams.attach: Button: attach the typed stream channel to the event.
tournament.streams.goTo: A link after the error saying another event already holds this channel. {name} is that event's name.
tournament.streams.handle.label: Accessible name of the field for a stream channel's name.
tournament.streams.handle.placeholder: Placeholder of the field for a stream channel: its name or its address.
tournament.streams.intro: Intro to the Streams settings. OBS is streaming software; a browser source is how it shows a web page. The overlay is the page drawn over the stream.
tournament.streams.none: When the event has no streams.
tournament.streams.overlays.help: Under the OBS overlay URLs heading. OBS is streaming software; a browser source is how it shows a web page.
tournament.streams.overlays.title: Heading over a stream's overlay addresses. OBS is streaming software.
tournament.streams.popOut: Link that opens a stream's queue in its own window. {handle} is the channel's name.
tournament.streams.producerOnly: Under a stream whose queue the viewer cannot run. The Streamer is a role an event host gives someone.
tournament.streams.remove.label: Accessible name of the button that detaches a stream from the event; {handle} is the stream's handle.
tournament.streams.route.label: Accessible name of the switch that sends this tournament's sets to one stream. {handle} is the channel's name.
tournament.streams.route.off: For a viewer without the switch: this stream is not taking this tournament's sets.
tournament.streams.route.on: For a viewer without the switch: this stream is taking this tournament's sets.
tournament.streams.route.this: Beside the switch that sends this tournament's sets to a stream.
tournament.streams.several: Shown when the event has more than one stream. The camera button is on each set.
tournament.swiss.bye: Beside a player who sits the round out; the dot leads.
tournament.swiss.nextRound.note: Explainer in that band; {next} is the round about to be paired, {total} how many rounds the stage plays.
tournament.swiss.projected: Tag beside that heading: the round is a projection, not played.
tournament.swiss.round1: Heading of the projected first round.
tournament.swiss.roundComplete: Label of the band offering the next Swiss round; {round} is the round just finished.
tournament.tiebreak.fifthSeventh.note: Explainer of the 5th- and 7th-place tiebreak option.
tournament.tiebreak.label: Heading of the tiebreaks band, and the format field's tiebreaks option.
tournament.tiebreak.remove.confirm: Confirmation question before removing a tiebreak; {reported} is yes when it has a result that goes with it.
tournament.tiebreak.remove.reason.off: Why a tiebreak needs a decision: the stage no longer plays tiebreaks; mid-line, lower case.
tournament.tiebreak.remove.reason.untied: Why a tiebreak needs a decision: the pair it was staged for is no longer tied; mid-line, lower case.
tournament.top8.notEnough: The Top 8 graphic page when fewer than four places are recorded.
tournament.trace.clear: Button that stops highlighting a player's path.
tournament.trace.gamesRecord: Under the highlighted player: their game record. `<b>` wraps the word, shown faint.
tournament.trace.of: After the highlighted player's place: out of how many. `{field}` is a number.
tournament.trace.out: One set in the highlighted player's run: it knocked them out.
tournament.trace.run: Accessible name and tooltip of the control that highlights an entrant's path through the bracket; {name} is the entrant.
tournament.trace.sets: Accessible name of the highlighted player's sets.
tournament.trace.setsRecord: Under the highlighted player: their set record. `<b>` wraps the word, shown faint.
tournament.trace.step: One set in the highlighted player's run: who they beat or lost to, and the score.
tournament.trace.tracing: Small label over the name of the player being highlighted.
tournament.vod.add: Button saving a new VOD link.
tournament.vod.add.more: Button opening the form adding another VOD; the plus sign is part of the label.
tournament.vod.group.official: Heading of the tournament's own broadcast recordings.
tournament.vod.group.playerRun: Heading of recordings following one player's run.
tournament.vod.group.restream: Heading of recordings by other channels.
tournament.vod.heading: Heading of a set's list of VODs (recorded videos).
tournament.vod.kind: Label of the picker choosing what kind of VOD it is.
tournament.vod.kind.official: VOD kind: the tournament's own broadcast.
tournament.vod.kind.playerRun: VOD kind: recorded by a player.
tournament.vod.kind.restream: VOD kind: a third party's restream.
tournament.vod.label: Accessible name of a VOD's label field.
tournament.vod.label.optional: Placeholder of a VOD's optional label field.
tournament.vod.link: Accessible name of the VOD link field.
tournament.vod.link.hint: Placeholder of the VOD link field.
tournament.vod.platform.link: A VOD hosted anywhere other than YouTube or Twitch.
tournament.vod.platform.twitch: The platform name; change only if it is written differently in your language.
tournament.vod.platform.youtube: The platform name; change only if it is written differently in your language.
tournament.vod.remove.confirmTitle: Question asked before a recorded video is taken off the tournament page; {name} is its title or, failing that, its platform.
tournament.vod.remove.keep: Cancel button of the remove-VOD dialog: keep the VOD.
tournament.walkUp.add: A walk-up is an attendee with no account, entered by staff at the venue.
tournament.walkUp.handle: The label of the field for the name a player competes under.
tournament.walkUp.prefix: The label of the optional team or sponsor prefix before a handle.
tournament.yourMatch.advancing: Heading of the viewer's match card while they wait for the next stage.
tournament.yourMatch.eliminated: Heading of the viewer's match card once they are out.
tournament.yourMatch.next.inQueue: The viewer's next set is ready, with other sets ahead of it on its stream.
tournament.yourMatch.next.upNext: The viewer's next set is the next to be played.
tournament.yourMatch.noSet: Heading of the viewer's match card when they have no set yet.
tournament.yourMatch.now.onStream: The viewer's set is being played on stream now.
tournament.yourMatch.now.playing: The viewer's set is being played now.
tournament.yourMatch.outFinished: Status on the viewer's own match card once they are eliminated; {wins} and {losses} are their record.
tournament.yourMatch.record: Read by screen readers before a player's wins–losses figures.
tournament.yourMatch.sitTight: Status on the viewer's own match card when nothing is queued for them.
tournament.yourMatch.throughTo: Status on the viewer's own match card when they have qualified for a stage that has not begun; {stage} is that stage.
tournament.yourMatch.waiting: The viewer's opponent is not decided yet.
